actions.name: Employ network segmentation

actions.name: Routing Access Mediation
actions.description: Routing access mediation is a network security approach that manages and controls access at the network layer using VPNs, tunneling protocols, firewall rules, and traffic inspection to ensure secure and efficient data routing.
actions.reason: Routing Access Mediation controls network layer access, enforcing secure data routing policies within the architecture.

actions.name: Directional Network Link
actions.description: Enforce one-way network communication by preventing two-way communication.
actions.reason: Directional Network Links enforce one-way communication, preventing reverse traffic and enhancing isolation capabilities.

actions.name: End-to-end encryption
actions.description: Implement end-to-end encryption (e.g., TLS, HTTPS) to protect the integrity and confidentiality of communications between AI systems.
actions.reason: End-to-end encryption protects data in transit, aligning with secure communication requirements for the network architecture.

actions.name: Network Access Mediation

actions.reason: Controlling access to systems over networks prevents unauthorized interactions with critical infrastructure components.

actions.name: Network Resource Access Mediation

actions.name: System Mapping
actions.description: System mapping encompasses the techniques to identify the organization's systems, how they are configured and decomposed into subsystems and components, how they are dependent on one another, and where they are physically located.
actions.reason: System mapping directly contributes to establishing architecture diagrams by identifying systems, their decomposition into components, dependencies, and physical locations.

actions.name: System Dependency Mapping
actions.description: System dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of system components on each other to carry out their function.
actions.reason: System dependency mapping models dependencies between system components, which is essential for creating detailed architecture diagrams showing inter-component relationships.

actions.name: Data Exchange Mapping
actions.description: Data exchange mapping identifies and models the organization's intended design for the flows of the data types, formats, and volumes between systems at the application layer.
actions.reason: Data exchange mapping models data flows between systems, a critical element for architecture diagrams depicting information flow and integration points.

actions.name: Logical Link Mapping
actions.description: Logical link mapping creates a model of existing or previous node-to-node connections using network-layer data or metadata.
actions.reason: Logical link mapping creates node-to-node connection models, directly supporting network architecture diagrams by visualizing logical connectivity.

actions.name: Organization Mapping
actions.description: Organization mapping identifies and models the people, roles, and groups with an organization and the relations between them.
actions.reason: Organization mapping models people, roles, and group relations, contributing to high-level architecture diagrams that include organizational structure and responsibilities.

actions.name: System Dependency Mapping
actions.description: System dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of system components on each other to carry out their function.
actions.reason: System dependency mapping directly supports maintaining architecture diagrams by modeling component interdependencies, which is essential for accurate system representation.

actions.name: Operational Dependency Mapping
actions.description: Operational dependency mapping identifies and models the dependencies of the organization's activities on each other and on the organization's performers (people, systems, and services.)  This may include modeling the higher- and lower-level activities of an organization forming a hierarchy, or layering, of the dependencies in an organization's activities.
actions.reason: Operational dependency mapping helps maintain architecture diagrams by documenting how organizational activities and systems interrelate, ensuring alignment with operational needs.

actions.name: Inventory Management
actions.description: Maintain an up-to-date inventory
actions.reason: Inventory management ensures up-to-date records of assets and components, which is critical for maintaining accurate and current architecture diagrams.

OntoSecAI.name: Implement Security Control during hardware manufacturing

actions.name: Hardware-based Process Isolation
actions.description: Preventing one process from writing to the memory space of another process through hardware based address manager implementations.
actions.reason: Hardware-based Process Isolation directly prevents interference between administrative processes and other system processes, ensuring dedicated resources for administrative work.

actions.name: Implement resource isolation techniques
actions.description: Implement resource isolation techniques, such as virtualization and containerization, and monitor resource usage to prevent manipulation that could lead to denial of service or data leakage in shared environments.
actions.reason: Resource isolation techniques like virtualization create dedicated environments for administrative tasks, aligning with the goal of dedicated computing resources.

actions.name: System Call Filtering
actions.description: Controlling access to local computer system resources with kernel-level capabilities.
actions.reason: System Call Filtering isolates administrative processes from system resources, restricting their access to only necessary functions and ensuring dedicated resource usage.

actions.name: Access Policy Administration
actions.description: Access policy administration is the systematic process of defining, implementing, and managing access control policies that dictate user permissions to resources.
actions.reason: Access Policy Administration defines policies to ensure only authorized entities can use administrative resources, enforcing dedicated allocation.

actions.name: Network Resource Access Mediation
actions.description: Control of access to organizational systems and services by users or processes over a network.
actions.reason: Network Resource Access Mediation isolates administrative systems from general network traffic, ensuring dedicated network resources for administrative work.
